title: Level 3 (Advanced) - D-5
notes:
West leads the ♥4 against 3NT. Its seems natural to play a low heart from dummy at trick 1, but in the above layout that would be a fatal mistake. East would win the ♥K and switch to a spade. West would win and clear the suit. West would later win a trick with the ♣K and cash the setting trick in spades.

South can guarantee the contract by winning West's heart opening lead with dummy's ♥A. South finesses in clubs, but when West wins the ♣K he cannot attack spades without giving South his 9th trick (South has already won a trick with the ♥A and can win 4 diamond tricks and 3 club tricks).

If West exits passively in a minor, South wins and plays the ♥Q to knock out the ♥K. East's spade return is covered by South and won cheaply by West. South's remaining spades are a stopper, however, as long as West is on lead.

If, instead of switching to a minor after winning the ♣K, West continues hearts, the result is the same. East wins the ♥K to play a spade, but South has his 9 tricks established and a certain stopper in spades (since East cannot gain the lead again).
